title: Two more digits. One less crisis.
summary: Stores loan years as four digits instead of two, so the year 2000 sorts and subtracts correctly.
caption: Artefact: a year, shown at full size for the first time.
footnote: Good until the year 9999. A future exhibit.

flow.label: Teller terminals
flow.detail:
Unchanged.
Tellers still type two digits.

arrow.label: Add the century
arrow.detail:
Years under 50 become 20YY.
The rest become 19YY.

risks.label: Wrong century guessed
risks.detail: A year typed as 49 becomes 2049, even when 1949 was meant.

flow.label: Loan records
flow.detail:
The year column grows from 2 digits to 4.
Old rows get a century by the same rule.

arrow.label: Read due dates
arrow.detail: The job now reads four-digit years.

parts.label: Old rows
parts.detail: Filled in once, by the same century rule.

risks.label: Fill stops halfway
risks.detail: Rows with two digits and rows with four would sit side by side.

work.label: Widen the year column
work.detail: Old programs still read the first two characters.

work.label: Fill in old rows
work.detail: Run on a copy first and compare balances.

flow.label: Nightly interest
flow.detail:
Counts days between dates.
With two digits, 2000 minus 1999 came out as −99 years.

arrow.label: Send entries
arrow.detail: Each interest entry carries a full year.

work.label: Read four-digit years
work.detail: Goes live the night the fill finishes.

flow.label: Statements
flow.detail:
Prints four-digit years.
Sorts by full year, so 2000 follows 1999.

work.label: Print four digits
work.detail: The layout gains two characters per date.

work.label: Compare a month of statements
work.detail: Old and new runs must agree on every balance.
